transcript.text: Good morning Rushil Bhatia. Here is your daily news for Monday, November 9. In today's briefing: top headlines, bhopal and madhya pradesh, business and markets, money, tax and personal finance, science and technology, development and policy, across india, around the world. Let's begin.

transcript.title: Top headlines
transcript.text: First, the stories leading the news this morning. Delhi's air quality slips into 'severe' category on Diwali; Mumbai's AQI at 170. Delhi experienced a significant decline in air quality overnight, with areas recording severe pollution levels. The Central Pollution Control Board reported an Air Quality Index of 406 at ITO, indicating hazardous conditions. Visibility was greatly reduced as a thick layer of smog enveloped the city during the early morning hours. Rajiv Chowk and South Extension also reported very poor air quality readings. Nvidia CEO admits affair with Chinese 'spy' Alice Huang; board orders security review. Nvidia's CEO, Jensen Huang, has made a public admission regarding his extramarital affair with Alice Huang of Megaspeed, acknowledging the ramifications for both his family and colleagues. An email from him outlined these concerns. Concurrently, Nvidia's board initiated an independent investigation over potential national security risks tied to Megaspeed, rumored to have links with Chinese espionage. Nevertheless, they continue to support Huang's leadership amidst the turmoil. Diwali crackers cure several diseases: BJP MLA. BJP's Tollygunge MLA Papia Adhikari made claims linking firecrackers to curing diseases during a Kali Puja inauguration. The chief minister, Suvendu Adhikari, emphasized the importance of bursting firecrackers during festival celebrations. He also urged the public to use eco-friendly or green crackers and comply with noise regulations. The significance of firecrackers was highlighted as essential to the Kali Puja festivities. 'Immigration policy too tough': 5 key takeaways from Trump's 60 minutes interview. Donald Trump admitted in a recent interview that the Iran war and deportation policies affected Republican midterm results. He acknowledged that while strong border security was supported, harsh deportation measures raised concerns among voters. Trump expressed a willingness to negotiate with Democrats on immigration reform, particularly for long-term residents. He maintained that Iran was prevented from obtaining nuclear weapons during his presidency, asserting military involvement in the region. Microsoft employees call work 'joyless' in open letter as 60,000 get buyout offers. Microsoft employees are circulating an open letter accusing the company of pursuing AI at all costs, saying work there has become "joyless and demoralizing." The letter is gaining attention after Microsoft offered buyouts to 60,000 employees across India, the US, UK and Canada, its largest ever. It flags forced AI use, layoffs, data centres and climate goals, as staff report raises below 1 percent while Microsoft posts a 32 percent profit jump. Parth meets Sharad Pawar twice in two days, NCP leaders seek to revive merger talks. Parth Pawar met Sharad Pawar for two consecutive days, raising speculation about a potential merger of NCP factions. Many senior leaders expressed discontent with how key decisions were made recently without their consultation. Meetings with Union home minister Amit Shah sparked additional concerns about intra-party disagreements within the NCP. Praful Patel announced he would meet Sharad Pawar after November 10 to discuss party matters. 'Pregnancy is not a disease': Bengaluru mom applies lipstick during labour. Myra Sharma from Bengaluru and Patna applied lipstick during labor to keep herself occupied. She explained that this personal choice helped her manage discomfort and maintain a sense of self. Understanding labor pain is variable, she acknowledged that every woman's experience is different. Myra shared her perspective on personal freedom during pregnancy and childbirth in her Instagram post. Arshdeep, Gurnoor Brar, Auqib Nabi to stay back for India's Test preparations. India has decided to retain pacers Arshdeep Singh, Gurnoor Brar, and Auqib Nabi for Test preparations. Batting coach Sitanshu Kotak stated that the ODI series conditions have been beneficial for the upcoming Test matches. A preparatory camp for Test players is scheduled to begin on November 11, which will help them get ready. Meanwhile, India leads the ODI series against New Zealand 2-0 after a close win in Wellington. In Noel's crosshairs, Chandra and Mehli reconnect at Tata HQ. Fresh from Italy, where Tata Motors announced the acquisition of commercial vehicle maker Iveco, Tata Sons chairman N Chandrasekaran invited Mehli Mistry, the late Ratan Tata's confidant and a trustee of the Tata Education and Development Trust, to Bombay House on Thursday. Woman spends $110,000 on home with partner; court rejects claim after split. After her relationship concluded, Mary Roth pursued the return of over $110,000 she invested in home enhancements. However, the North Dakota Supreme Court determined that she could not secure restitution through an unjust enrichment claim. The ruling underscored that Roth needed to demonstrate an actual financial benefit to the property owner, something her receipts failed to do when it came to increasing the property's market value. Grandmother raised grandson from infancy; court bars joint adoption with partner. In a landmark decision, North Dakota's Supreme Court ruled that unmarried couples are barred from adopting a child together, as dictated by existing state law. This case involved a grandmother and her partner who intended to adopt her grandchild, with agreement from both biological parents. The court clarified that only legislative changes can alter adoption laws, while allowing individual adoption requests from either of the parties involved.
